_sections_note: MEASURED against live codex 0.139.0 (2026-06-15). The old footer anchor (tab to queue message|⏎ send|^[›>]$) matched NOTHING this codex renders, so footer defaulted to the whole screen and every `until: footer` section (modal/body/options/status) collapsed to EMPTY — the FSM could never see the approval modal or the Working spinner and sat in idle forever. The modal section now anchors directly on its own landmark with NO `until` (the guard regexes are modal-specific, so a whole-screen fallback in non-modal frames is harmless). body is the whole screen (Working/esc-to-interrupt only appear while generating). See docs/guides/CLI_SPEC_MEASURED_REWRITE.md.

_statustail_note: STATUS-TAIL-REANCHOR history + CODEX-LONG-OUTPUT-BUSY-SIGNAL supersession (2026-08-15). History: status_tail was originally a landmark-less from_bottom:12; because the FSM viewport is blank-trimmed (ghostty-vt-backend getText -> trimBlankEnds), from_bottom counted from the LAST NON-BLANK line, so long output filled the window and the live spinner escaped ABOVE it. That was re-anchored to the composer landmark (^\u203a\s, anchor_last) with above:12. SUPERSEDED: `above:K` sets from=anchor-K but leaves to=TOTAL (evaluator.ts resolveSections), so the section was never a bounded window -- it was '12 lines above the composer PLUS everything below it'. More importantly the composer anchor does not pin the spinner: codex renders the live status line directly above the composer only on SHORT turns; once output is long the spinner scrolls far above the composer (or the composer is absent mid-turn, where anchor_miss:empty made status_tail EMPTY). Measured on the real background-tool.pty fixture through the real ghostty backend: status_tail was EMPTY on every frame of the stream while `Working (8s \u00b7 esc to interrupt)` was plainly on the grid. Every spinner leaf therefore read 'no spinner' DURING generation -- the busy->idle vetoes were disarmed, which is why the FSM left busy only via the 30s elapsed fallback. status_tail is now BOUNDED (above:12 + lines:13 => [anchor-12, anchor+1)) so it means what its name says, and it is no longer used for the spinner veto at all.
_selfmatch_note: SPINNER-BODY-SELFMATCH (still enforced, by a different mechanism). The busy cues used to be checked as unanchored literals against whole-screen `body`; assistant prose quoting codex's own spinner self-matched -> busy latched forever. The previous fix scoped the cues to a narrow status_tail, but that traded SELFMATCH for the long-output blindness described in _statustail_note -- the two failure modes pull in opposite directions, which is why this defect kept recurring across fixes. The cue is now scoped WHOLE-SCREEN (section `screen`, matching provider.v1.json tui.spinner.scope = 'whole-screen', which was already live-verified for this provider) and SELFMATCH is prevented by the cue SHAPE instead of the window: the regex anchors to the START of a line because codex renders the spinner as its OWN status line while prose embeds it mid-sentence. The optional leading decoration run is ANY 1-2 non-word, non-space chars (braille, bullet, bar, middot -- codex has shipped several spinner glyphs; a braille-only prefix would silently miss the others, which is the same class of failure this defect is about) EXCLUDING quote/backtick/markdown/bracket openers, which are prose, never spinner glyphs. The bare `\u00b7 esc to interrupt)` alternative was REMOVED from the cue -- measured, it is the alternative that prose actually matches, and it is redundant since codex always renders it on the same line as `Working (`/`Thinking (`. Residual, accepted: a wrapped prose line that happens to begin with `Working (12s` can still match. That fails SAFE (holds busy, released by the 30s elapsed fallback), unlike the pre-fix direction (premature idle mid-turn, which has no backstop).
_busyidle_fallback_note: BUSY-IDLE-BOUNDED-FALLBACK (CODEX-FSM-BUSY-WEDGE RCA, 2026-07-26). Live evidence: a completed session (final response + composer `› …` returned) sat in busy for 22+ min with busy→idle firing 0 times; mesh debug showed condResult=false with remainingMs≈1342 on the all(3), which only the stable_ms leaf can produce (regex/not leaves report 0) — a benign post-generation repaint inside the cursor_above:4 window kept resetting regionLastChangedAt every frame, faster than stable_ms=1500 (fsm-driver.ts trackRegionChanges). The wake scheduler kept re-evaluating; the stable clock simply never accumulated. busy→idle is now an `any` of two arms: arm 1 is the ORIGINAL strict guard, byte-equivalent (not tail spinner, not MCP-init, stable 1500/cursor_above 4) so quiet completions still idle at ~1.5s; arm 2 is a bounded fallback — the same spinner/MCP-init vetoes PLUS a modal veto (regex synthesized from the →approval/→trust/→picker transition patterns above to avoid drift) PLUS elapsed_ms:30000 — so once every active marker (Working|Thinking spinner, esc to interrupt, MCP init, trust/approval/picker modal) is absent for 30s since busy entry, idle commits even if the stable window never settles. Safety invariants: a live spinner, MCP init, or any modal vetoes BOTH arms (no false idle during generation/approval); the fallback never consults transcript signals (final_assistant_present is NOT used) so transcript unavailability changes nothing. During a >30s generation the live spinner keeps arm 2 vetoed; modal appearances are additionally caught by the priority 100/110 →approval/→trust/→picker transitions before either arm matters.

_longoutput_note: CODEX-LONG-OUTPUT-BUSY-SIGNAL / MESH-WORKER-REPORT-SELFMATCH (2026-08-15). REPORTED SYMPTOM: a mesh-delivered task showed INFINITE GENERATING and its result never reached the coordinator; a spec-debug snapshot showed busy held 855023ms, escaping only via `elapsed 855023ms / 30000ms`. ROOT CAUSE (read the snapshot leaves literally): `not regex status_tail~/.../ = FALSE` means the spinner cue MATCHED. Both busy->idle arms carry that same veto, so while the matching text was on screen NEITHER arm could fire and busy was PINNED -- the 855s is not 'waiting for a signal', it is how long the offending text stayed in the window; `elapsed` (long since >=30s) committed the instant the text scrolled out. WHAT MATCHED: the old cue accepted any DIGIT directly after the paren, so ordinary delegated-worker report prose -- `Working (3 packages) rebuilt cleanly`, `Thinking (2 steps)`, `Working (12 files) verified` -- read as a live spinner. This is why it reproduced under MESH task delivery (workers emit structured reports full of such phrases) and effectively never in a hand-driven session. FIX: the paren must contain an actual DURATION (12s / 2m 14s / 1h 3m / 45ms / h:mm) or a braille animation glyph -- never a bare count. Line-anchoring alone is NOT sufficient: worker reports are bulleted/indented lists, so the phrase sits at line start where a position-only guard still admits it. The 30s `elapsed_ms` arm is DELIBERATELY RETAINED as the safety net; without it a judgement failure means permanent busy. Turn START (idle->busy, mcp_init->busy, approval->busy) uses the same cue and was verified unbroken. NOTE on direction: an earlier pass on this defect mis-read the snapshot as the OPPOSITE failure (premature idle from a spinner scrolling out of a narrow window). The section geometry findings from that pass are real and retained (see _statustail_note), but they were NOT the reported bug -- this note records the mechanism that actually produced the infinite generating.
